blocks.text: 1. RAG Architecture
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707474-89914131.png
Parametric vs Non-Parametric Memory closed by pointing here. RAG Architecture expands the simple two-stage picture into the real components built from these two kinds of memory.
It lays out every component a real RAG system needs, end to end.
2. Recapping The Preview
RAG architecture was previewed in that earlier topic as mapping out the full system built from two memory types.
This topic maps that system out in full.
3. Recapping The Two Stages Again
Retrieval and generation, covered in What Is RAG, are the two headline stages of any RAG system.
A real architecture breaks each of those stages into several smaller, concrete components.
4. The Ingestion Pipeline Component
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707475-774916251.png
Before any query even arrives, an ingestion pipeline prepares the document collection in advance.
It loads and processes raw content, the first concrete component, covered in more depth under Document Ingestion.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Architecture component","When it runs"],"rows":[["Ingestion pipeline","Before any query arrives, prepared in advance"],["Retriever","At query time, on every incoming request"]]}

blocks.text: 5. The Chunking Component
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707475-919986633.png
Raw documents get split into smaller, searchable pieces before embedding.
That splitting is the second concrete component, and gets a full, dedicated module of its own later, in Chunking.
6. The Embedding And Index Components
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707475-945902452.png
Each chunk then gets converted into an embedding, the technique covered in Embeddings.
Those embeddings then get stored in a vector database for fast later search, the third and fourth components in the pipeline.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: These two components set up Vector Databases, a later dedicated module in this course, which explores exactly how that storage and search works under the hood.

blocks.text: 7. The Retriever Component
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707476-495049286.png
At query time, a retriever component embeds the query and searches the index.
This is the retrieval using embeddings described back in What Is RAG, and it returns the top matching chunks as the fifth component.
8. The Generator Component
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707476-95552752.png
The generator component then combines the query with those retrieved chunks into one prompt.
Using the prompting techniques covered earlier, this lets a language model produce the final answer, the sixth and final component.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Component","Role in the full architecture"],"rows":[["Retriever","Finds the most relevant chunks for a given query"],["Generator","Produces the final answer from query plus retrieved chunks"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Optional Re-Ranking Component
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785446707476-379412536.png
Many real systems insert an optional re-ranking step between retrieval and generation.
Why Re-Ranking, a later dedicated module in this course, explores that refinement step, an optional but common seventh component.
10. Recognizing Why A Full Architecture View Matters Beyond The Simple Two Stage Picture
A full RAG architecture reveals many separate places where quality can be improved.
For a small, simple prototype, the minimal two stage RAG described in What Is RAG remains sufficient.
11. Worked Example
The example below demonstrates the full RAG architecture as one connected pipeline of components.

code.content:
# splitting a raw document into chunks
raw_document = "The company was founded in 2015. It expanded to Europe in 2019. Revenue grew steadily since."
chunks = [c.strip() for c in raw_document.split(".") if c.strip()]

def embed(text):
    # a simplified stand-in for a real embedding function
    return [len(text), text.lower().count("e"), text.lower().count("a")]

# building the index from chunk embeddings
chunk_index = [(chunk, embed(chunk)) for chunk in chunks]

def retrieve(query, index, top_k=1):
    # the retriever: embed the query and find the closest chunks
    query_embedding = embed(query)
    scored = [(chunk, sum((a - b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(query_embedding, emb)) ** 0.5) for chunk, emb in index]
    scored.sort(key=lambda item: item[1])
    return [chunk for chunk, distance in scored[:top_k]]

def generate(query, retrieved_chunks):
    # the generator: combine query and retrieved chunks into an answer
    context = " ".join(retrieved_chunks)
    return f"Based on: '{context}' -> Answer to '{query}' is grounded in that retrieved context."

query = "When did the company expand to Europe?"
retrieved = retrieve(query, chunk_index)
print(f"Chunks: {chunks}")
print(f"Retrieved: {retrieved}")
print(f"\nFinal answer: {generate(query, retrieved)}")

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows every architecture component working together in sequence, from raw text through chunking, embedding, retrieval, and finally generation.

blocks.text: 12. Common Mistakes

items: Treating RAG as just two stages when a real system has several distinct, tunable components.
Forgetting that ingestion and chunking happen before any query, not at query time.
Skipping the index component and assuming embeddings alone are enough for fast search.
Assuming re-ranking is mandatory rather than an optional refinement step some systems add.

blocks.text: 13. Key Takeaways

items: RAG architecture breaks the two headline stages into several smaller, concrete components.
An ingestion pipeline prepares the document collection before any query ever arrives.
Chunking splits raw documents into smaller, searchable pieces before embedding.
Embedding and indexing convert chunks into vectors and store them for fast search.
The retriever embeds the query and searches the index to find the most relevant chunks.
The generator combines the query with retrieved chunks into one prompt for the final answer.
Many real systems add an optional re-ranking step between retrieval and generation.
A full architecture view reveals many separate places where a RAG system can be improved.
